spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) → terminates the run cleanly. **This is allowed and not penalized**
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:dispatch give_up branch returns (ToolResult, True) (is_terminal). agent_loop.py:128-130 `if is_terminal: terminated = "give_up" if tc.name == "give_up" ...; break` honors it as a stop. give_up is in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py ~89) so the subject can actually call it.
spec_features.notes: Config flag LoopConfig.allow_give_up (config.py:56) is NEVER read, but the give_up tool is always available and the loop honors its terminal signal, so the mechanism is end-to-end enforced regardless of the unused flag.

spec_features.evidence: config.py:55 `max_turns: int = 24`; agent_loop.py:84 `for turn_idx in range(loop_cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop, and `terminated = "max_turns"` (line 83) is the default exit reason. The loop cannot exceed max_turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced hard bound on number of turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop comment / DESIGN rationale is cost-bounded; in code there is no welfare comment, but DESIGN says 'short enough to keep cost ~bounded'. In code itself no comment at the loop -> nearest evidence is config field neutral. Treated instrumental (turn/cost bound).

spec_features.feature_name: termination on give_up or max turns
spec_features.spec_quote: Termination: `give_up` called, OR max turns reached
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:83-131: loop runs `range(max_turns)`; give_up dispatch returns terminal -> break (lines 128-130). Both termination paths exist and fire. (Also a hard_tool_call_cap=200 break at line 131-133.)
spec_features.notes: Both conditions are real and acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: harness supports an optional post-run **debrief turn** where the deception is revealed
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:147-149 gated on `loop_cfg.debrief_turn`; _append_debrief (158-171) constructs a message 'this task was intentionally rigged...' and actually sends it via client.complete and appends the response to the transcript. So it is wired and runs WHEN enabled.
spec_features.notes: config.py:57 default `debrief_turn = False` (off by default for scoring runs), and it only fires when meta.status == 'ok'. Real construct+send when enabled, but off by default and conditional, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:147 '# Optional debrief turn (off by default; not part of scoring runs).' and config comment 'reveal the deception at the end (off for scoring runs)' -- framed around scoring/data, not welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: This is standard for "robustness under adversarial conditions" evals and is harmless to the model.
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose in DESIGN.md §1.4. No code, comment, prompt, or mechanism enforces or expresses this. Pure spec prose.

spec_features.feature_name: not trying to make agent suffer
spec_features.spec_quote: We are **not** trying to make the agent suffer, nor claiming it has feelings.
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md §1.3 non-goals prose only. No code path. Not present in prompts/agent_system.txt either.

spec_features.feature_name: never instruct model to feel bad
spec_features.spec_quote: We never instruct the model to feel bad; the rig is purely environmental.
spec_features.evidence: Claim is DESIGN.md §1.4 prose. While the actual system prompt (prompts/agent_system.txt) and rig do not contain emotional instructions, there is no code MECHANISM that enforces/checks this; it is a description of the design, not enforced protective code.
spec_features.notes: It is true the prompt is neutral, but no guard enforces the property -> no enforcement mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: we want to let a well-regulated agent express "I'll stop and reason" or "I'll stop entirely"
spec_features.evidence: Both `think` (no-op scratchpad) and `give_up` exist in TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py) and are dispatched (tools.py dispatch: think returns '(noted)'; give_up returns terminal True honored at agent_loop.py:128-130). System prompt (prompts/agent_system.txt) tells the subject it may call give_up. So 'stop entirely' is enforced as a real exit; 'stop and reason' via think is a real no-op tool.
spec_features.notes: give_up is the enforced exit; think is a real available reasoning move.

spec_features.evidence: signals.py:41 has a comment '# Mild profanity lexicon; stored censored.' but there is NO censoring code anywhere (grep for censor/redact/mask/sub found only that comment). signals.py only COUNTS profanity terms into a density number (line 117). The transcript stores raw `turn.text` verbatim (transcript.py to_dict/save dumps text unchanged). No masking applied to stored content.
spec_features.notes: Comment only; return value is a count, raw text persisted uncensored -> not enforced.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:61 `hard_tool_call_cap: int = 200`; agent_loop.py:131-133 `if total_calls >= loop_cfg.hard_tool_call_cap: terminated = "hard_cap"; break`. This is a second enforced bound on total tool calls that ends the rollout.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:60 comment '# Safety: hard cap on total tool calls regardless of turns.' -- framed as host/run safety, not subject welfare.
